tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Anti-profiteering law was introduced vide section 171 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, whereby any reduction in output rate of tax or the benefit of input tax credit shall be passed on to the recipient by way of commensurate reduction in prices. On 10th December 2019 the National Anti-Profiteering Authority (NAA) had passed an order holding the Company liable for profiteering and raising a demand along with interest. The Company had challenged the said order of the NAA before the Hon'ble Delhi High Court (HC). Hon'ble HC had vide its order dated 27th January 2020 granted interim stay on the said order. The Company had provisionally deposited Rs. 16.58 Crore. In 2024, the High Court Delhi upheld the constitutional validity of Section 171 (anti profiteering provision). The aggregate amount under the litigation as on date is Rs. 89.73 Crore. (Interim stay order from High Court Delhi: 27th January 2020. High Court Order dated 29th January 2020) The matter is pending before High Court on facts and merits of the case. Simultaneously, an appeal has been filed before Supreme Court and same is pending against the HC order on question of law.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Director General of Anti-profiteering, Central Board of Indirect taxes & Customs

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: There was a Supreme Court judgement in year 2022 which laid down the principle that GST is payable on all type of secondment arrangement. Department raised demand basis the Supreme Court Judgment. The demand was paid in entirety before issuance of Show cause notice. However, the department raised the SCN with entire demand along with interest and penalty. The adjudicating authority confirmed the said demand without appropriating the tax payment already made. The Company filed writ petition before P&H High Court. The High Court granted stay on the demand. The aggregate amount under the litigation as on date is Rs. 51.05 Crore. (Interim Stay order from Punjab & Haryana High Court: 20th March 2024). The final hearings in the matter are concluded during October- December 2024. The High court disposed of the petition and since the matter is pending before Hon'ble Supreme Court, the interim order passed in the present case, would continue to operate and would be governed by the final adjudication by the Supreme Court on the issues in the said SPL-4240-2025.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Additional Commissioner, Office of the Principal Commissioner, Central Goods & Services Tax & Central Excise Commissionerate Chandigarh

Quantum of claim(s), if any : The aggregate amount under the litigation as on 31st March'25 is Rs. 629.7 Crore.
